routes.name: I want to use AI well
routes.for: No coding. You want to understand what these tools are and get far more out of them.

routes.name: I want to build with AI
routes.for: You can code a little (or want to) and plan to make apps, automations and agents.

routes.name: I want to understand and train models
routes.for: You want to know how models work inside, build one, and train or fine-tune your own.

stages.title: Start here: what AI actually is
stages.blurb: No maths, no code. A clear mental model of what a neural network and a language model are, what they are good and bad at, and how people really use them.
stages.outcome: You can explain in plain words how a chatbot produces an answer, and you know where it can't be trusted.

items.title: Large Language Models explained briefly
items.why: The best short visual explanation of what an LLM is doing. Watch this first.

items.title: Intro to Large Language Models
items.why: A one-hour general-audience talk covering how LLMs are made, where they are heading and their security problems.

items.title: But what is a neural network?
items.why: Builds the idea of a neural network from scratch with animation instead of equations.

items.title: Elements of AI
items.why: A gentle, text-based course for complete beginners on what AI is and isn't. No programming needed.

items.title: Generative AI for Everyone
items.why: A non-technical tour of what generative AI can do at work and how projects are run. Free to audit.

items.title: How I use LLMs
items.why: A practical walk through everyday use: search, files, voice, images, code and custom assistants.

stages.title: Using AI well: prompting and everyday practice
stages.blurb: Getting good results is a skill. These teach you to give clear context, structure a request, check the output and know when to push back.
stages.outcome: You can write a prompt that reliably gets what you want, and diagnose why one didn't.

items.title: Anthropic Academy: AI Fluency and Claude 101
items.why: Free no-code courses on working with AI effectively and responsibly. Start with AI Fluency.

items.title: Prompt engineering interactive tutorial
items.why: Nine chapters with exercises, from basic structure to complex prompts. The most thorough free prompting course.

items.title: Prompt engineering overview
items.why: A concise reference of the techniques that matter, in order of impact.

items.title: Prompt engineering guide
items.why: OpenAI's own strategies and tactics. Worth reading alongside Anthropic's to see what is common to both.

items.title: ChatGPT Prompt Engineering for Developers
items.why: A short video course with notebooks. Good first step from chatting to calling a model from code.

items.title: Prompt Engineering Guide
items.why: An encyclopaedia of prompting techniques with examples and the papers behind them.

items.title: Prompt Engineering
items.why: A research-grounded survey of why techniques like few-shot and chain-of-thought work.

stages.title: Foundations: Python, maths and classic machine learning
stages.blurb: The groundwork for everything technical that follows. You need less maths than you fear: vectors, matrices, derivatives and probability, plus enough Python to run a notebook.
stages.outcome: You can train and evaluate a simple model on real data and explain what overfitting is.

items.title: Python
items.why: The fastest route to enough Python for ML, in the browser with nothing to install.

items.title: Essence of linear algebra
items.why: Gives you the geometric intuition for vectors and matrices that every later topic leans on.

items.title: Essence of calculus
items.why: Derivatives and the chain rule, which is all backpropagation is.

items.title: Machine Learning Crash Course
items.why: A well-paced introduction with interactive exercises, covering regression through to neural nets and LLMs.

items.title: Intro to Machine Learning
items.why: You build and validate a real model within the first hour.

items.title: StatQuest video index
items.why: Patient, step-by-step explanations of nearly every statistics and ML concept. Look things up here when stuck.

items.title: CS50's Introduction to Artificial Intelligence with Python
items.why: Search, logic, probability, optimisation and learning, each with a substantial programming project.

items.title: CS229: Machine Learning (lectures)
items.why: The full mathematical treatment of classical ML, for when you want the derivations.

items.title: Mathematics for Machine Learning
items.why: The standard free textbook for the maths. Use it to fill specific gaps, not to read cover to cover.

stages.title: Deep learning: how neural networks learn
stages.blurb: Neural networks, backpropagation and training loops. By the end you will have written a network by hand and trained real ones in PyTorch.
stages.outcome: You can build, train and debug a neural network in PyTorch and read a loss curve.

items.title: Neural networks (full series)
items.why: Gradient descent and backpropagation made visual. Watch before writing any code.

items.title: Neural Network Playground
items.why: Train a tiny network in your browser and watch what layers, neurons and learning rate actually do.

items.title: The spelled-out intro to neural networks and backpropagation
items.why: You build an autograd engine from nothing. Backpropagation stops being magic after this.

items.title: Practical Deep Learning for Coders
items.why: Top-down and practical: you train a state-of-the-art model in lesson one and learn the theory as you go.

items.title: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
items.why: The bottom-up counterpart to fast.ai. Everything is coded live from first principles, ending in a GPT.

items.title: Learn the Basics
items.why: The official tour of tensors, datasets, models and the training loop.

items.title: 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
items.why: A fast, up-to-date lecture series with labs, refreshed every year.

items.title: CS231n: Deep Learning for Computer Vision
items.why: The classic rigorous course. Its notes and assignments are still some of the best written on the fundamentals.

items.title: Dive into Deep Learning
items.why: A free interactive textbook with runnable code for every concept.

stages.title: How language models are built
stages.blurb: Tokens, embeddings, attention and the transformer. You go from pictures, to an interactive model you can poke, to writing a GPT yourself.
stages.outcome: You can explain the transformer block by block and have built and trained a small GPT.

items.title: Transformers, the tech behind LLMs
items.why: The clearest visual walk through what happens to your text inside a transformer.

items.title: Attention in transformers, step-by-step
items.why: Attention is the key idea. This is the explanation that makes it click.

items.title: Transformer Explainer
items.why: A live GPT-2 in your browser. Type text and watch every step of the computation.

items.title: LLM Visualization
items.why: A 3D walkthrough of a small GPT, showing every matrix as it runs.

items.title: The Illustrated Transformer
items.why: The article that taught a generation of engineers the architecture.

items.title: Deep Dive into LLMs like ChatGPT
items.why: The whole pipeline end to end: data, tokenisation, pre-training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning and why models hallucinate.

items.title: Let's build GPT: from scratch, in code, spelled out
items.why: You write a working transformer line by line. The single most valuable two hours in this programme.

items.title: Let's build the GPT Tokenizer
items.why: Tokenisation explains many odd model behaviours. Here you build one.

items.title: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch): code and videos
items.why: The full code for the book, free, with notebooks for every chapter from attention to fine-tuning.

items.title: The Annotated Transformer
items.why: The original paper, implemented line by line next to the text.

items.title: Attention Is All You Need
items.why: The paper that introduced the transformer. Readable once you have done the items above.

items.title: CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
items.why: The academic backbone of the field, with lecture videos, notes and assignments online.

items.title: CS336: Language Modeling from Scratch
items.why: The deepest free course on building an LLM: tokeniser, architecture, GPU training, data and scaling. Demanding.

stages.title: Training and fine-tuning your own models
stages.blurb: Using open models, adapting them to your own data, and knowing when fine-tuning beats a better prompt (often it doesn't).
stages.outcome: You can fine-tune an open model on your own dataset, evaluate it and run it.

items.title: LLM Course
items.why: The practical handbook for the open-model ecosystem: loading, tokenising, fine-tuning, evaluating and sharing models.

items.title: Finetuning Large Language Models
items.why: A short orientation on when to fine-tune, how to prepare data and how to evaluate the result.

items.title: Fine-tuning guide and notebooks
items.why: Ready-to-run notebooks that fine-tune current open models on a free GPU. The quickest way to do it for real.

items.title: smol course
items.why: A hands-on course on post-training small models: instruction tuning, LoRA, evaluation and synthetic data.

items.title: PEFT: parameter-efficient fine-tuning
items.why: The library and concepts behind LoRA and friends, which make fine-tuning affordable.

items.title: LLM Course
items.why: A curated roadmap with notebooks, split into fundamentals, the LLM scientist and the LLM engineer.

items.title: Let's reproduce GPT-2 (124M)
items.why: A real training run from an empty file: optimisation, mixed precision, distributed training and evaluation.

items.title: nanochat
items.why: A complete, readable ChatGPT-style pipeline you can train yourself on rented GPUs: tokeniser, pre-training, fine-tuning and a web UI.

stages.title: Building applications: APIs, retrieval and evaluation
stages.blurb: Most useful AI products are a model plus your data plus careful checking. This stage covers calling models from code, retrieval (RAG), and the unglamorous work of measuring whether it is any good.
stages.outcome: You can ship a small app that answers questions over your own documents, and prove it works with an eval.

items.title: Anthropic courses: API fundamentals, tool use and more
items.why: Notebook courses that take you from a first API call through real-world prompting, evaluations and tool use.

items.title: OpenAI Cookbook
items.why: Hundreds of worked examples for common tasks. Search it before building anything from scratch.

items.title: Claude Cookbooks
items.why: Copy-and-adapt recipes for retrieval, tool use, structured output, vision and agents.

items.title: Generative AI for Beginners
items.why: A lesson-by-lesson course on building generative AI apps, with code in Python and TypeScript.

items.title: RAG From Scratch
items.why: Short videos and notebooks that build retrieval up one idea at a time: indexing, query rewriting, routing and re-ranking.

items.title: LLM University
items.why: Particularly strong on embeddings, semantic search and retrieval.

items.title: Your AI Product Needs Evals
items.why: The essay that made evaluation the centre of applied AI work. Read before you ship anything.

items.title: What We Learned from a Year of Building with LLMs
items.by: Yan, Bischof, Frye, Husain, Liu & Shankar
items.why: Hard-won practical lessons from six practitioners, covering tactics, operations and strategy.

items.title: Patterns for Building LLM-based Systems & Products
items.why: Seven recurring patterns (evals, RAG, fine-tuning, caching, guardrails and more) and when each applies.

items.title: LLM Bootcamp
items.why: Lectures on the full lifecycle of an LLM product. From 2023, so tool names have dated, but the thinking has not.

stages.title: Agents and agentic workflows
stages.blurb: Models that use tools, take multiple steps and act on your behalf. This is the fastest-moving stage, so it mixes durable principles with current tools: MCP, coding agents and agent frameworks.
stages.outcome: You can design, build and supervise an agent that completes a real multi-step task, and you know when a simple workflow is the better choice.

items.title: Building effective agents
items.why: The essential starting point: the difference between workflows and agents, the common patterns, and why to keep it simple.

items.title: Claude Code in Action
items.why: A free hands-on course on working with a coding agent. The quickest way to feel what agentic work is like.

items.title: Claude Code: best practices for agentic coding
items.why: Habits that carry over to any coding agent: give context, plan first, verify, and run work in parallel.

items.title: AI Agents Course
items.why: Widely recommended as the best free structured course: agent fundamentals, tool calling, several frameworks and a final build.

items.title: AI Agents for Beginners
items.why: Lessons with runnable code on design patterns, tool use, planning, multi-agent systems and taking agents to production.

items.title: Model Context Protocol: introduction
items.why: MCP is the standard way to connect agents to tools and data. The official docs include build-a-server tutorials.

items.title: MCP Course
items.why: A hands-on course that has you building and deploying MCP servers and clients.

items.title: 5-Day AI Agents Intensive
items.why: A self-paced guide pairing a whitepaper with hands-on labs each day, from first agent to evaluation and deployment.

items.title: Introduction to LangGraph
items.why: A free course on one widely used agent framework: state, memory, human-in-the-loop and deployment.

items.title: A practical guide to building agents
items.why: OpenAI's view of when to build an agent, how to design tools and guardrails, and single versus multi-agent setups.

items.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
items.why: What goes into the context window decides how well an agent performs. Covers compaction, memory and sub-agents.

items.title: Writing effective tools for agents
items.why: Most agent failures are tool-design failures. How to design, describe and evaluate tools.

items.title: 12-Factor Agents
items.why: Engineering principles for agents that are reliable enough for production, written by people shipping them.

items.title: LLM Powered Autonomous Agents
items.why: The foundational survey of planning, memory and tool use. Older, but still the clearest map of the ideas.

stages.title: Going deeper: research, interpretability and safety
stages.blurb: For when you want to read papers, understand what happens inside models, or work on making them safe. Pick what interests you; nobody does all of it.
stages.outcome: You can read a current paper, reproduce a result, and find your way into a research area.

items.title: Paper explanations
items.why: Careful walk-throughs of important papers. A good way to learn how to read them yourself.

items.title: CS25: Transformers United
items.why: A seminar series where leading researchers present current work on transformers.

items.title: ARENA curriculum
items.why: A rigorous free programme of exercises on transformers, interpretability, reinforcement learning and evaluations.

items.title: Getting started in mechanistic interpretability
items.why: A concrete on-ramp into reverse-engineering what networks have learned.

items.title: Transformer Circuits Thread
items.why: The primary research on how features and circuits form inside language models.

items.title: AI safety courses
items.why: Free, well-regarded courses on AI alignment and governance, with open curricula.

items.title: Diffusion Models Course
items.why: How image generation works, from the theory to fine-tuning and guiding your own models.

items.title: Spinning Up in Deep RL
items.why: A compact introduction to reinforcement learning with clean reference implementations.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Course
items.why: Theory plus practice training agents in games. No longer actively maintained, so some later units may not run.
